title: Materialization can write outside the working directory
reasoning: InputFile paths are joined to cwd without containment validation. Absolute paths discard cwd, parent traversal escapes it, and existing symlinks can redirect writes outside it. A caller-controlled input path can therefore overwrite files accessible to the process outside the intended working directory.
reproduction: Materialize a TEXT InputFile whose path is '../outside.txt' into a temporary working directory; the file is written in its parent.
recommendation: Reject absolute and escaping paths and enforce destination containment, including symlink handling, before creating directories or opening files.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: The included tests cover metrics and language registration, not input-file destination containment.
suggestedRegressionTest: Exercise ordinary nested paths, absolute paths, parent traversal, and symlink escapes; assert rejected destinations leave outside files unchanged.

history.reasoning: The evidence path and lines still exist. entrypoint.py:336-350 now rejects absolute paths and checks resolved destination containment before directory creation or writing, addressing traversal and existing symlink escapes. tests/execution/file_ops_test.py:585-633 covers nested paths, absolute paths, traversal, symlink escapes, and unchanged outside content.
